papers.title: High density cell seeding affects the rheology and printability of collagen bioinks.
papers.abstract: An advantage of bioprinting is the ability to incorporate cells into the hydrogel bioink allowing for precise control over cell placement within a construct. Previous work found that the printability of collagen bioinks is highly dependent on their rheological properties. The effect of cell density on collagen rheological properties and, therefore, printability has not been assessed. Therefore, the objective of this study was to determine the effects of incorporating cells on the rheology and printability of collagen bioinks. Primary chondrocytes, at densities relevant to cartilage tissue engineering (up to 100 × 106 cells ml-1), were incorporated into 8 mg ml-1 collagen bioinks. Bioink rheological properties before, during, and after gelation as well as printability were assessed. Cell-laden printed constructs were also cultured for up to 14 d to assess longer-term cell behavior. The addition of cells resulted in an increase in the storage modulus and viscosity of the collagen before gelation. However, the storage modulus after gelation and the rate of gelation decreased with increasing cell density. Theoretical models were compared to the rheological data to suggest frameworks that could be used to predict the rheological properties of cell-laden bioinks. Printability testing showed that improved printability could be achieved with higher cell densities. Fourteen-day culture studies showed that the printing process had no adverse effects on the viability or function of printed cells. Overall, this study shows that collagen bioinks are conducive to bioprinting with a wide range of cell densities while maintaining high printability and chondrocyte viability and function.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了细胞密度对胶原生物墨水流变性和可打印性的影响，但未涉及任何AI方法。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not embed AI into any bioprinting workflow stage; it is a purely experimental rheology and printability study without machine learning or autonomous decision-making.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究细胞密度对胶原生物墨水流变性和可打印性的影响。
summary_zh.method: 制备不同细胞密度的胶原生物墨水，测量流变特性并进行打印测试。
summary_zh.result: 高细胞密度提高了打印性，但降低了凝胶后的储能模量。
summary_zh.validation: 通过流变测试、打印评价和14天细胞培养验证。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate how cell density affects the rheological properties and printability of collagen bioinks for cartilage tissue engineering.
summary_en.method: Collagen bioinks with varying chondrocyte densities (up to 100×10^6 cells/ml) were characterized rheologically before, during, and after gelation, and printability was assessed via extrusion-based bioprinting.
summary_en.result: Higher cell densities increased pre-gelation viscosity and storage modulus but decreased post-gelation storage modulus and gelation rate, while improving printability.
summary_en.validation: Rheological measurements, printability testing, and 14-day in vitro culture with viability and functional assays.

papers.title: Sodium Alginate/Gelatine Hydrogels for Direct Bioprinting-The Effect of Composition Selection and Applied Solvents on the Bioink Properties.
papers.abstract: Hydrogels tested and evaluated in this study were developed for the possibility of their use as the bioinks for 3D direct bioprinting. Procedures for preparation and sterilization of hydrogels and the speed of the bioprinting were developed. Sodium alginate gelatine hydrogels were characterized in terms of printability, mechanical, and biological properties (viability, proliferation ability, biocompatibility). A hydrogel with the best properties was selected to carry out direct bioprinting tests in order to determine the parameters of the bioink, adapted to print with use of the designed and constructed bioprinter and provide the best conditions for cell growth. The obtained results showed the ability to control mechanical properties, biological response, and degradation rate of hydrogels through the use of various solvents. The use of a dedicated culture medium as a solvent for the preparation of a bioink, containing the predicted cell line, increases the proliferation of these cells. Modification of the percentage of individual components of the hydrogel gives the possibility of a controlled degradation process, which, in the case of printing of temporary medical devices, is a very important parameter for the hydrogels' usage possibility-both in terms of tissue engineering and printing of tissue elements replacement, implants, and organs.

llm.why_not_core: This paper does not use AI/ML methods; it is purely experimental hydrogel characterization without any intelligent algorithm or data-driven optimization.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发适合直接生物打印的海藻酸钠/明胶水凝胶生物墨水。
summary_zh.method: 通过调节组分和溶剂系统表征水凝胶的可打印性、力学和生物学性能。
summary_zh.result: 确定了最佳生物墨水配方，能控制力学性能、降解率和细胞增殖。
summary_zh.validation: 通过打印测试和细胞实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: To develop sodium alginate/gelatine hydrogel bioinks suitable for direct bioprinting.
summary_en.method: Characterized printability, mechanical, and biological properties by varying composition and solvent systems.
summary_en.result: Identified an optimal bioink formulation that controls mechanical properties, degradation rate, and cell proliferation.
summary_en.validation: Validated through printing tests and cell-based assays.
